Name: Super Star Valley - Music Replacer
Author: Stacked4ths
Description:
[color=#b6b6b6][size=4][u][i][b]NOTE: [/b][/i]This mod is incomplete. Most tracks are replaced, but it is still a work in progress. Send in any song suggestions in the comments. I am also including instructions + a video tutorial on how to add to this mod if you want to![/u][/size][/color]

[size=4][b]Description[/b][/size]
[size=3][color=#D4D4D8]   This mod replaces the music of Stardew Valley with music from the classic era of 3D Mario. I am a huge fan of the Sunshine, Galaxy, and 3D World games, and I also love Stardew. I couldn't find any up-to-date music replacement frameworks, so here I am with this. Instructions for adding on to it will be below.[/color][/size]

[size=4][b]Installation / Requirements[/b][/size]
[size=3][color=#D4D4D8]   This mod uses Content Patcher, so you will have to have that first. Otherwise, it shouldn't interfere with much else.[/color][/size]

[b][color=#ff00ff][size=5]How to edit the music yourself:[/size][/color][/b]
[size=4]   Because of the relatively simple nature of this mod, it is pretty easy to change to your liking. Here's how.[/size]

1. Go into the mod folder and open the content.json. It should look like this.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/56048/56048-1795658440-15080456.png[/img]

^ 
2. Choose which song you'd like to replace and [color=#ffd966]find its [u]sound ID/cue ID[/u][/color] (ID that triggers the song to play) using this list: [url=https://stardewvalleywiki.com/Modding:Audio#Track_list]https://stardewvalleywiki.com/Modding:Audio#Track_list[/url] 

3. If the sound is already replaced in my mod, search for that sound ID in the content.json. From there, you can use this format to replace the sound:

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/56048/56048-1795658440-580390260.png[/img]

^
4. In order to replace the sound with your own music, you will need to [color=#ffd966]get your own audio file.[/color] I personally use youtube or this website: [url=https://downloads.khinsider.com/]https://downloads.khinsider.com/[/url] 
Then, I use an audio editing software (Audacity) to [u][color=#ffd966]convert the sound file to a .ogg file![/color][/u] I also use the [i]normalize loudness[/i] function and bring the percieved loudness down to about -17.5 LUFs. You don't have to do this, but it helps the track blend in better.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/56048/56048-1795659160-487951559.png[/img]      <--- (Loudness Normalization in Audacity)

5. After you have your .ogg file, name it something easy to type and [u][color=#ffd966]put it into this mod's "assets" folder.[/color][/u]

6. Back in the content.json, reroute the file path to your own .ogg file by [color=#ffd966]replacing the file name[/color] for that particular sound ID. 

As seen below:

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/56048/56048-1795658440-2100471367.png[/img]

   And that's it! Unless...

[color=#6aa84f][size=5][b][i]What if the song I want to replace isn't already in the content.json???[/i][/b][/size][/color]
[color=#6aa84f][size=5][b][i]+ VIDEO TUTORIAL[/i][/b][/size][/color]

[color=#ffffff][size=4]    You will need to complete steps 1, 2, 4, and 5, then [u]add your own entry to the json using this template and tutorial:[/u][/size][/color]

[size=4][color=#6d9eeb]"SOUNDID":{
"ID":"SOUNDID",
"Category":"Music",
"FilePaths": [ "{{AbsoluteFilePath: assets/FILENAME.ogg}}" ],
            "StreamedVorbis": true,
            "Looped": true
},[/color][/size]

[color=#ffffff][size=4][u][youtube]2XNzx2I9R6U[/youtube][/u][/size][/color]

[color=#ffffff][size=4][u]Please comment if you have any questions! This mod is a WIP but it is going to be completed eventually.[/u][/size][/color]
